messages.subject: auto_write=TRUE only works for cores > 1?
parts:
Hi all

Thank you the new release of stan, it brings some nice features! Especially rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE), was a welcome addition. However, I can only get it to work when the cores argument is larger than 1. Is this intentional?

I have attached a small script which shows the behavior.

Here is my system info and I have reproduced the behavior on an ubuntu virtual machine.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: auto_write=TRUE only works for cores > 1?
parts:
On Tuesday, August 4, 2015 at 4:02:49 AM UTC-4, Per Nielsen wrote:
Thank you the new release of stan, it brings some nice features! Especially rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE), was a welcome addition. However, I can only get it to work when the cores argument is larger than 1. Is this intentional?

I'm not sure what you mean. When I run it, it auto_writes a .rda model to tempdir() the first time it is called and reads it without recompiling the second time. If you do it in a new R session, the temporary directory is erased and it has to auto_write .rda model again the first time the first time it is called.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: auto_write=TRUE only works for cores > 1?
parts:

As the output shows, the code is compiled each time I loop, but something is changing in the temp (I did the ls command a few times during the loop). If I set cores = 2 in stan, I get the output from R_console_cores_2.txt, where it clearly does not compile.

Maybe I have some system setup issues?

Can you try installing rstan from GitHub?
